## Attention( $ Q, K, V $) = softmax  $ \left(\frac{QK^{T}}{\sqrt{d_{k}}}\right)V $

## Why is naive attention slow?

- Materializes the full score matrix $S = QK^{T}$ and probability matrix $P = \text{softmax}(S)$

- High HBM traffic: write S, read S, write P, read P

- Time and memory grow quadratically with sequence length: O(N^{2})

 $$ S=Q K^{T},\quad P=softmax(S), $$ 

 $$ O=P V $$ 

## FlashAttention: built on two ideas

### 1. Tiled GEMM

Compute QK^{T} and PV block by block instead of materializing the full N  $ \times $ N matrix.

blockwise $Q_{i}K_{j}^{T}$

### 2. Online Softmax

Maintain running statistics while scanning blocks:

 $$ (m_{A},d_{A})\oplus(m_{B},d_{B})=(m,d_{A}e^{m_{A}-m}+d_{B}e^{m_{B}-m}) $$ 

## Why faster?

No full attention matrix in HBM

• Much lower memory traffic

Exact attention, not approximation
